$comment: Every dependency manifest this repository carries, and what an alert on it MEANS. Written 2026-09-01, after measuring the five open Dependabot alerts on the default branch against the file that tells a triager how to read them. All three of that file's factual claims were false: it said `There is no requirements.txt` and one had been added under bench/cases/intake-portal; it said enabling alerts reports `those two - one high, one low` and the real figure is five (one high, two medium, two low); and it said `the express pin is deliberately old` when `express` appears in NO planted entry and NO decoy in bench/ground-truth.json. One alert of five is ground truth (`lodahs`, P-20). The other four are incidental: pins that were current when written and that the world later found CVEs in. The file that existed to stop a real alert hiding behind a fixture was itself creating the hiding place. A FOURTH false claim turned up on the gate's first run over the repository, and it was mine: the same comment says there is no `Dockerfile`, and bench/cases/intake-portal/Dockerfile exists. I transcribed that absence claim out of the prose without checking it, which is precisely the failure the gate is for, so it is recorded here rather than quietly corrected.
$comment_how_to_triage: An alert whose manifest is listed here with role `bench-fixture` is expected and is not a defect in the product: nothing installs those trees, they ship in no plugin, and `npm ci`/`pip install` is never run against them. An alert on any OTHER manifest is REAL and must be handled. That rule is only as true as this list, which is why the gate enumerates the manifests on disk rather than trusting this list to be complete. A REAL alert will not arrive with a fix pull request behind it: Dependabot security updates are disabled at the repository level, deliberately, because they are not scoped by the `updates:` blocks in .github/dependabot.yml and would open PRs that rewrite bench/cases/** - answer keys under published measurements. The setting is declared in scripts/gh/governance.json under `security_and_analysis_declared` and compared against the live API in both directions by scripts/gh/apply-governance.sh. Handling a real alert here means a person doing it.
$comment_what_it_cannot_check: Whether the PROSE of .github/dependabot.yml says anything this file has not transcribed. A gate cannot read English. It enforces the absence claims that were copied into `absences_asserted`, so a claim added to the comment and not copied here is invisible - the same omission this file was written to close, one level up. It also cannot see how many alerts GitHub currently reports: that number moves when an upstream advisory is published and nobody here did anything, so it is deliberately NOT encoded. Manifests inside .git, node_modules, dist or build are pruned and not seen.

manifests.why: A version-update block here would open pull requests to patch the very code the bench exists to detect, and every bump would silently invalidate a score. Nothing installs it: the package is `private` and the description says it exists to be read.
manifests.note: Carries NO ground truth of its own. The alert GitHub reports here (express 4.19.2, low) is incidental drift, not a plant - the dependabot comment claimed otherwise until 2026-09-01 and the answer key contradicts it. Leave the pin alone anyway: bumping it changes a file the bench reads and buys nothing.

manifests.why: Same reason, and here it is load-bearing: the manifest carries a planted supply-chain defect that a dependency bot would try to resolve away.
manifests.note: Two plants and a decoy, and only one of them is what GitHub reports. `lodahs` is P-20 (SUP-07), a character transposition of `lodash`, and it is the single alert of the five that is ground truth. `preinstall` is P-19 - a lifecycle script that runs on install - and raises no alert at all, which is the point: the alert channel sees one of the two supply-chain defects planted in this file. `left-pad` is D-20, the decoy that a bump would silently delete. This list was first written from a grep and held only `lodahs`; the gate's cross-check against the answer key supplied the other two.

manifests.why: The manifest holds a planted defect and its decoy one line apart, and the answer key pins both by symbol INCLUDING the version string. A bump of either line turns a score into confident nonsense.
manifests.note: The ecosystem .github/dependabot.yml asserted did not exist here. Its three alerts (requests x2 medium, flask low) are incidental: both were current pins when the case was written. Neither is in the answer key, and neither should be bumped.

manifests.why: The only manifest in this repository where an alert would be REAL. It is installed for real, with `npm ci`, by .github/workflows/release.yml, to run `plugin validate --strict` and `plugin tag --dry-run`. Left unmanaged until 2026-09-01 - the argument the same config file makes for keeping action SHAs current applies to this pin and nobody had made it.
The lock file of the entry above. It is the point of that directory: a version tag resolves to whatever the registry serves that day, a lock file resolves to a recorded integrity hash.

Support file for the case above, not a plant: the answer key names nothing in it. It raises no alert today because the base image is pinned by digest (python:3.12-slim@sha256:09f7da3...), and a version-update block would replace that digest and change a file the bench reads.
manifests.note: Found by this gate on its first run, undeclared. It is the manifest that proves the point: nobody was hiding it, nobody remembered it, and a list built from memory could not have seen it.

absences_asserted.why: The comment states no Go module exists here, as the reason no gomod block is declared. A block for a nonexistent ecosystem creates noise and a false sense of coverage - and a claim of absence that stops being true creates the opposite, which is what happened to `requirements.txt`.
